title: Soil Resources Flashcards
description: Key facts from TNPSC Group II Geography Soil Resources Chapter

cards.q: What are the four main components of soil?
cards.a: Mineral particles, humus, water, and air.

cards.q: Which soil horizon is known as the transition zone?
According to the USDA soil taxonomy, which soil order covers the largest area in India (39.74%)?
What are the two types of alluvial soils found in the Upper and Middle Ganga plains?
What are the calcareous concretions found in Khadar and Bhangar soils called?
Alluvial soils are generally rich in which nutrient but poor in phosphorous?
What is the alternative name for Black Soil?
cards.a: Regur Soil or Black Cotton Soil.

cards.q: What characteristic of Black Soil causes it to develop wide cracks during the dry season?
cards.a: It shrinks when dried, leading to a 'self-ploughing' character.

cards.q: Black soils are chemically rich in lime, iron, and magnesia, but lack which three major components?
What causes the reddish colour in Red Soils?
cards.a: A wide diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks.

cards.q: The word 'Laterite' is derived from the Latin word 'Later', which means what?
What process is primarily responsible for the formation of Laterite soils in high rainfall areas?
cards.a: Intense leaching (lime and silica are leached away).

cards.q: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala are highly suitable for which tree crop?
What layer in the bottom horizons of Arid Soils restricts the infiltration of water?
In areas of the Green Revolution like Punjab and Haryana, what is added to the soil to solve the problem of salinity caused by excessive irrigation?
Peaty soils, found in areas of heavy rainfall, can contain up to what percentage of organic matter?
In which year was the National Green Tribunal Act enacted?
